stories.summary: The deep divisions between nations over climate finance, which contributed to the breakdown of COP31 talks, underscored the funding challenges facing African countries as they try to adapt to a warming planet. Although the continent contributes only 4% of global emissions , nine of the 10 most climate-vulnerable countries are in Africa , according to one study. In 2022, the continent received far less than the $190 billion required annually in climate funding, and its biggest economy alone needs more than $15 billion to fully implement climate adaptation policies over the next decade. While South Africa is experiencing heat waves that are damaging agricultural output, its grid remains heavily reliant on the sorts of fossil fuels that contribute the most to global emissions. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

stories.summary: Thanksgiving dinner might be killing you. No, this isn’t a column introducing the newest internet diet fad based on sketchy science and scare tactics. It isn’t about the food at all. It’s actually about the people around the table. According to new research conducted at several American universities and published earlier this year , hanging around negative people can literally make you age faster. articles.summary: The News White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is out and is being replaced by Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies, multiple officials told Semafor Thursday . The shakeup follows a series of disruptive tech outages that have raised fears about US cybersecurity — and has kicked off a heated dispute about whether Cairncross was fired or left voluntarily. One White House official and a person familiar with the White House told Semafor that Cairncross was fired on Thursday; the official said that finding a new cyber director was one of the first things Stephen Miller did in his new role as White House chief of staff, and both said Trump had supported Cairncross’ removal. But another senior White House official and a person familiar with the matter strongly disputed the idea that Cairncross had been fired, telling Semafor that he resigned — and not because he was asked to. A second source familiar with the matter, who said Cairncross had been fired, said the past week exposed the need for someone “more competent, with the expertise needed to execute this position.” Axios first reported the news of Cairncross’ departure and Davies’ new job.
